The second DEV set confirms the direction, at a smaller size. SC gives +2.0 ± 2.4 on dev_b2 (22 wrong→right, 17 right→wrong) with cut-offs down from 29.7% to 21.5%. Pooled over both DEV sets (512 problems) the gain is about +3.3 ± 1.8 points, positive in both, so SC is a credible but modest improvement.

With 35 passes left, I'll check whether a stronger loop component helps before freezing. C(-1.5) freed only about half of the loops. A larger dose could free more but might also suppress legitimate restating. That risk showed in the 9 right→wrong pairs. A teacher-forced screen is the cheap way to see where the damage begins, so I'll screen C(-3.0) alone on the same 750 texts and compare with C(-1.5) (pass 12). If onsets fall much further (say P(onset) below 0.45) while finished answers and references stay within about 0.02 nats per token, I'll run SC with C(-3) on the DEV sets. If the damage grows quickly, C(-1.5) stays and I'll freeze SC.

C(-3.0) alone is saved, and SC remains backed up in /work/best_SC. This teacher-forced screen on the same 750 texts shows how far a double dose moves the onset decision and whether finished answers and references start to suffer.

Pass 16 for C(-3.0) is done. The per-text means fell a bit more than at -1.5, by about 0.015 to 0.03. I'll put the same table for C(-3.0) next to C(-1.5): onset logprob, same-token novel lines, in-loop tokens, finished answers and references.

Doubling the dose roughly doubles the effect on loops, but selectivity gets worse:

| Change vs original | C(-1.5) | C(-3.0) |
|---|---|---|
| Onset first token | -0.44 | -0.96 |
| P(onset) | 0.60 | 0.49 |
| In-loop tokens | -0.11 | -0.37 |
| Same-token novel line starts | -0.12 | -0.36 |
| Finished answers (per token) | -0.005 | -0.018 |
| References (per token) | +0.011 | 0.000 |

So ordinary reasoning tokens are barely affected, but C(-3) noticeably discourages normal line starts as well. That could either free more loops or disturb good answers, and only generation can tell. I'll build SC3: S(1.0) composed with C(-3.0) in the same way as SC. I'll run it on dev_b1 and then dev_b2, so its pooled DEV gain can be compared with SC's +3.3 ± 1.8 on the same 512 problems. I'll adopt SC3 only if it is clearly better, around +5 or more pooled. Otherwise SC, the milder and more selective edit, stays the candidate.
